title: König's Cofinality Constraint from Mathlib API
description: Proves cf(2^aleph_0) > aleph_0 from Mathlib's Cardinal.lt_power_cof, replacing the axiomatized version. The key is (2^aleph_0)^aleph_0 = 2^aleph_0 combined with König's inequality.

meta.author: König (1905), formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib

mathlibDependencies.description: König's inequality: κ < κ^cf(κ) for infinite κ

openQuestion: Can König's constraint cf(2^ℵ₀) > ℵ₀ be proved from Mathlib's cofinality API rather than stated axiomatically?
significance: Eliminates an axiom from the parent formalization. König's cofinality constraint is the strongest ZFC-provable restriction on the continuum: it rules out 2^ℵ₀ = ℵ_ω and any other cardinal with countable cofinality. Combined with Easton's theorem, it gives the complete characterization of possible values.

overview.historicalContext: Julius König proved his cofinality inequality in 1905, showing that the continuum cannot be expressed as a countable supremum of smaller cardinals. This was one of the earliest ZFC-provable constraints on the size of the continuum, predating even the precise formulation of ZFC. Kurt Gödel (1940) and Paul Cohen (1963) showed the Continuum Hypothesis is independent of ZFC, but König's constraint survives as a genuine theorem. William Easton (1970) proved the converse: König's constraint is the ONLY restriction ZFC imposes on the continuum — for any regular cardinal $\kappa \geq \aleph_1$, there is a model of ZFC with $2^{\aleph_0} = \kappa$. This file proves König's constraint from Mathlib's `Cardinal.lt_cof_power`, eliminating an axiom from the parent formalization and giving the complete picture of what ZFC says about the continuum.
overview.problemStatement: Can König's constraint $\text{cf}(2^{\aleph_0}) > \aleph_0$ be proved from Mathlib's cofinality API (`Cardinal.lt_cof_power`), replacing the axiomatized version in the parent file? Can we additionally characterize which alephs are permitted and which are excluded as values of the continuum?
overview.proofStrategy: The proof proceeds in four parts: (1) apply `Cardinal.lt_cof_power` directly to get the core König constraint in one line; (2) compute cofinalities of specific alephs (successor alephs are regular, $\text{cf}(\aleph_\omega) = \aleph_0$); (3) derive excluded values via contradiction (if $2^{\aleph_0} = \kappa$ with $\text{cf}(\kappa) \leq \aleph_0$, then König is violated); (4) verify permitted values (regular cardinals $\kappa > \aleph_0$ satisfy König because $\text{cf}(\kappa) = \kappa > \aleph_0$).
keyInsights: König's constraint follows from Mathlib in one line: `Cardinal.lt_cof_power le_rfl (by norm_num)` — what was axiomatized in the parent is a theorem

The excluded values are precisely the cardinals with countable cofinality: $\aleph_\omega$, $\aleph_{\omega \cdot 2}$, $\aleph_{\omega^2}$, etc. — these are the limit alephs indexed by ordinals of countable cofinality

The permitted values are all regular uncountable cardinals: $\aleph_1$ (CH), $\aleph_2$ (PFA), every successor aleph $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$, and large regular limit cardinals like weakly inaccessible cardinals
König + Easton together give the complete ZFC characterization: $2^{\aleph_0}$ can be exactly any regular $\kappa \geq \aleph_1$, and nothing else — a rare case of a complete independence result
The `lt_irrefl` proof pattern for excluded values is elegant: substitute the hypothesis into König to get $\aleph_0 < \aleph_0$, which is absurd

sections.title: König's Cofinality Constraint
sections.summary: Proves cf(2^ℵ₀) > ℵ₀ from Mathlib's Cardinal.lt_cof_power in one line. Also proves the general form for arbitrary bases κ > 1.

sections.title: Cofinality Computations for Specific Alephs
sections.summary: Proves ℵ₁ and ℵ₂ are regular, all successor alephs are regular, and cf(ℵ_ω) = ℵ₀ (making ℵ_ω singular).

sections.title: Excluded Values
sections.summary: Proves 2^ℵ₀ ≠ ℵ_ω and 2^ℵ₀ ≠ any cardinal with cofinality ≤ ℵ₀, via contradiction with König.

sections.title: Permitted Values
sections.summary: Shows all regular uncountable cardinals satisfy König. Verifies ℵ₁, ℵ₂, and all successor alephs ℵ_{α+1} as permitted values.

sections.title: The Complete ZFC Picture
sections.summary: Packages both ZFC constraints (ℵ₁ ≤ 2^ℵ₀ and cf(2^ℵ₀) > ℵ₀) and proves ℵ_ω is the first excluded value.

conclusion.summary: This fully verified formalization (0 axioms, 0 sorries) proves König's cofinality constraint from Mathlib and gives the complete ZFC characterization of possible values for the continuum. The core result is a one-line proof from `Cardinal.lt_cof_power`, eliminating the axiom from the parent file. The formalization then classifies alephs as permitted (regular, like $\aleph_1, \aleph_2, \aleph_{\alpha+1}$) or excluded (singular with countable cofinality, like $\aleph_\omega$).
conclusion.implications: Combined with Easton's theorem (not formalized, as it requires forcing), this gives a complete independence result: ZFC constrains $2^{\aleph_0}$ to be a regular uncountable cardinal, and every such cardinal is consistent. This is one of the cleanest applications of Mathlib's cardinal arithmetic API, demonstrating that deep set-theoretic results can be expressed concisely in Lean 4.
openQuestions: Can Easton's theorem (consistency of 2^ℵ₀ = κ for regular κ ≥ ℵ₁) be formalized in Lean, or does it inherently require a meta-theoretic forcing construction?
Can the singular cardinal hypothesis (SCH) and its independence be formalized using Mathlib's pcf theory infrastructure?
Can the formalization handle the generalized continuum function 2^ℵ_α for all α, classifying the full Easton spectrum?
